Title: Trump says US 'low-keying it' with Iran
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump signaled Sunday he is prepared to let economic pressure mount against Iran, apparently backing away from ordering more military strikes even as Teheran issues tough demands.
"We are low-keying it," Trump said, according to the news outlet Axios, which said it spoke to him in a brief phone call.
Only a week ago Trump made the latest of his series of threats to hit Iran hard, only to back off, as he presses for a deal to end the war he started along with Israel on Feb 28.
Axios said Trump did not express any frustration Sunday with Iran's delaying an agreement to open up the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has demanded that the US first end its blockade of Iranian ports and lift oil sanctions, as per the memorandum of understanding the two countries signed in June.
The strait's blockage by Iran since the war started has sent fuel prices soaring and rattled the world economy, putting pressure on the Trump administration as midterm elections in November grow nearer.
"We are only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money," Trump was quoted as saying.
Trump also said oil prices are falling so American consumers are feeling less pain from the war.
"It will work out. It always works out. It's like a chess game," Trump said of US dealings with Iran.

Title: Airbus sees supply chain recovery as it targets 870 deliveries
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Airbus is confident that its supply chain is showing signs of recovery as the aircraft manufacturer works towards its target of delivering around 870 commercial aircraft this year.
Airbus Asia Pacific president Anand Stanley said the company is seeing improvements in multiple areas of its supply chain as it ramps up production.
"We are growing and stabilising our supply chain and we see improvements in multiple areas, which are facilitating the significant rate increase.
"We're also working closely and intensively with our partners, and the overall situation is much brighter now, and the number of irritants are getting fewer and better managed," he told Business in an exclusive interview recently.
In the recent Airbus half year 2026 results, the European planemaker said that it had delivered 351 commercial aircraft in the first half of 2026, up from 306 aircraft in the same period last year.
The deliveries comprised 44 A220s, 271 A320 Family aircraft, 10 A330s and 26 A350s.
Airbus chief executive officer Guillaume Faury said the company's first-half performance mainly reflects the higher level of commercial aircraft deliveries.
"Our focus on steady execution is paying off as demonstrated by strong deliveries in Q2. This fuels our confidence in our future performance, as reflected in the recently-communicated mid-term outlook," he said in a statement.
Gross commercial aircraft orders totalled 886 in the first half of 2026, compared with 494 aircraft in the same period last year.
Net orders stood at 821 aircraft after cancellations, while Airbus' commercial aircraft order backlog amounted to 9,222 aircraft at the end of June 2026.
According to Airbus' latest orders and deliveries data, the company delivered 89 aircraft to 49 customers in June 2026.
Stanley said Airbus delivered 81 aircraft to 45 customers in May 2026.
"This delivery number figure is nearly 60 per cent higher than May 2025 and when you look at the entire year of 2026 there has been an eight per cent increase in deliveries in 2026 versus the year before of 2025."
"This demonstrates a solid progress on the ramp up, so given this trajectory, we continue to work towards our target of around 870 aircraft this year," he said.
Airbus said its 2026 guidance assumes no additional disruptions to global trade or the world economy, air traffic, the supply chain, its internal operations and its ability to deliver products and services.
On that basis, the company is targeting around 870 commercial aircraft deliveries in 2026.
Despite the improvement, Stanley says Airbus is still working through supply chain constraints in several areas.
"We continue to see some supply chain issues on which we are working with our customers and our partners, but as I mentioned, the overall situation is much brighter now with fewer known irritants."
"They continue to be topics that we are working on, such as cabin equipment, aerostructures, and engines," he said.
Stanley said Airbus is also continuing with its broader production ramp-up plans across its aircraft programmes.
The A220 ramp-up is ongoing with Airbus continuing to target a monthly production rate of 13 aircraft in 2028.
For the A320 Family, Airbus expects to reach a rate of between 70 and 75 aircraft a month by the end of 2027, before stabilising at rate 75 after next year.
The company is also targeting to reach a rate of five aircraft per month for the A330 programme in 2029 and rate 12 aircraft monthly for the A350 programme in 2028.
"We continue to work beyond that towards our overall ramp-up plans and rates, such as stabilising at a rate of 75 for the A320 family beyond 2027 and to reach the rate of 13 per month for the A220 family in 2028, to reach the rate of five aircraft per month for the A330 in 2029 and to reach the rate of 12 aircraft per month for the A350 family in 2028," Stanley said.
He added that the ramp-up is tied to Airbus' work with suppliers and partners to meet long-term aircraft demand, particularly in Asia.
"All these are a result of our efforts to work with our partners in stabilising our supply chain more than anything else to meet the demand, especially in Asia for the 20,000 aircraft that we have to meet over the next couple of decades," he said.
Stanley also said Airbus is seeing strong order momentum from Asia-Pacific.
He added that Airbus recorded 815 gross orders in the first five months of 2026, including 379 orders in May alone.
"A large number of these orders, over 50 per cent of the global Airbus orders of 815, and the majority of the 379, are all from the greater Asia Pacific region, including China," he said.

Title: Over 200 firefighters battle blaze in southern France
Article:
MENDE, France: A fast-moving wildfire was raging in southern France on Sunday, forcing evacuations as more than 200 firefighters raced to contain the blaze.
The fire broke out around 12.45pm (1045 GMT) in the Lozere region, about 140 kilometres (85 miles) northwest of Montpellier.
Officials said it might have been sparked by a vehicle catching fire on a local road.
By late afternoon, the fire had burned some 153 hectares (370 acres) and continued to spread.
Around 270 firefighters from Lozere and neighbouring departments were deployed, backed by four Canadair water bombers and two Dash aircraft.
A Lozere fire service spokesman said their combined efforts had helped "contain the blaze and save two homes" that were directly threatened.
"The flanks are being held. Work is now focused on the head of the fire, which remains inaccessible," he added.
As a precaution, two hamlets in the municipality of La Tieule, directly in the path of the flames, were evacuated at around 5:00 pm, affecting about 20 homes.
"This is an area with a great deal of woodland. It's extremely dry. The drought is unlike anything we've seen in a long time," said Marc Toulouse, a senior fire officer in Lozere.
Local authorities urged residents not to call emergency services to report the blaze, warning that doing so could overload crews already fighting the fire.
French officials are still taking stock of the damage caused by a series of fires, mainly in the south of France, including largest wildfire since 1949, in the southwest Gironde region.

Title: Medan Selera 223 traders pin hopes on RM40.5m flood plan [WATCH]
Article:
PETALING JAYA: Traders at Medan Selera 223 are hoping that a RM40.5 million   flood mitigation plan will   end  costly  flash floods.
Work on the plan —  which brings together 39 projects —  began on Aug 1, and the head of the main traders' association in the area said they were looking forward to its completion.
"I am satisfied with what MBPJ presented because the plan was  clear," said Medan Selera PJ Lestari Traders Association chairman Farahanim Ahmad, 43.
The Petaling Jaya City Council's  (MBPJ) plan will, among others, involve high-capacity drainage upgrades, automated flood gates, runoff pumping
stations and an underground water detention pond to absorb  downpours.
The projects are being carried out in phases, with all scheduled to be completed by February.
"We believe these  steps will finally protect our livelihoods and bring long-term peace of mind," Farahanim said.
She said each flood could cost traders up to RM2,000 each due to damaged equipment and supplies.
"When a flood hits, everything has to be thrown away, from 10kg of cooked rice to meat and chickens.
"Appliances like blenders, gas stoves and electric rice cookers are  ruined."
Farahanim, who represents 20 of the 60 stalls at the food court, said not all were in operation as the financial impact of the floods had forced some traders to suspend operations temporarily.
She added that others  had given up their lots, leaving just 35 operating there.
She said the  majority of traders were adamant about staying put, as the area is  known  as an iconic food spot.
[[nid:1507812]]
For 57-year-old drinks trader S. Nesamalar,  the  cycle of floods has taken a  financial and emotional toll.
The  single mother  has operated at the food court for seven years,
"Every time it rains, I am scared. I keep thinking, 'What if my fridge spoils again? How am I going to repair it?'
"Cleaning up is no problem, but the things I have to buy are all expensive.
"As a single mother, it is very difficult. I just leave the fridge as it is because I do not know where to get the money to fix it again."
She expressed relief upon learning about MBPJ's  plans.
"I believe that once this project is complete, there will not be any more floods."
Petaling Jaya member of parliament  Lee Chean Chung, who facilitated a dialogue session with stakeholders, urged MBPJ and the Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) to carry out the engineering works swiftly.
He said that during the session, MBPJ explained that recent flash floods were triggered by intense  downpours measuring between 65mm and 104mm within a brief window.
"The  surge in surface runoff overwhelmed  drainage capacities, causing  Sungai Penchala and Sungai Klang to burst their banks."
Lee    told traders that business operations would continue without  forced relocations during the construction phase, with strict assurances given on safety and project delivery timelines.
"I will maintain oversight and hold MBPJ and DID  accountable to their commitments.
"We will monitor these   projects to ensure they are completed on time."
Lee  said  river desilting and maintenance works along Sungai Penchala must remain a  priority for  federal and state agencies to ensure long-term flood resilience.

Title: Gaza plan rejected by Netanyahu 'only way forward': Trump board head
Article:
JERUSALEM: The US-backed plan for Gaza rejected on Sunday by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remains the "only way forward" to prevent a repeat of Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack, the head of President Donald Trump's implementation board said.
"The option we are offering today is the only way forward that ensures this tragedy does not happen again," Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, said in an interview with Israel's Channel 12 television.
He said that further talks were underway and, "I hope these discussions will lead to a positive outcome for everyone."
Netanyahu earlier told his cabinet that he rejected the plan, under which Hamas would hand over weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing body and Israel would start a withdrawal from the war-ravaged territory.
Mladenov described the current stage of the agreement as a commitment involving the United States, Hamas and the Board of Peace – notably leaving out Israel.
He also reiterated an assurance he made to Netanyahu last week that Israel would pull out only after a complete Hamas disarmament, walking back earlier language that spoke of Israel starting a phased withdrawal.
But Mladenov maintained that Israel would eventually pull out if there were verified disarmament.
"If there is genuine demilitarisation, Israel will withdraw from the Strip," he said.
He said the disarmament would involve all Hamas weapons, down to Kalashnikov rifles.
Israel has demanded the destruction of all weapons, not just handing them over.

Title: 'Fewer South Koreans are eating kimchi'
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SEOUL: South Korean adults are eating less kimchi despite the growing global popularity of the country's signature side dish, Yonhap News Agency reported yesterday.
According to a joint study by researchers from Chung-Ang University, Jeju National University and the World Institute of Kimchi, the proportion of  Korean adults who reported eating no kimchi within the past 24 hours rose from 11.7 per cent in 2010 to 22.7 per cent in 2024.
The study was based on the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data from 2010 to 2024.
Non-consumption rates among men doubled from 10.2 per cent to 20.6 per cent, while rates for women climbed from 13.1 per cent to 24.8 per cent.
Across all age groups, except children under 10, the proportion of people eating kimchi as a standalone side dish declined.
The sharpest drop occurred among adults aged 20 to 39, where regular side-dish consumption fell from 82 per cent in 2010 to 66 per cent in 2024.
1:18 - Instead, kimchi is increasingly being used as an ingredient in other dishes, such as kimchi jjigae (spicy stew).
Socioeconomic factors also played a role: adults in the lowest-income bracket reported higher kimchi consumption than those in the highest-income group.
"The trend in kimchi consumption reflects broader changes in meal composition and eating habits," the research team said.
"Public health strategies for the future should move away from simply promoting kimchi consumption and shift to encouraging more balanced diets."

Title: Demand for Japanese cuisine lifts exports to Malaysia
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The warm reception to Japan's cuisine will boost its agricultural and seafood exports to Malaysia, said Japan External Trade Organisation (Jetro) Kuala Lumpur managing director Koichi Takano.
"Malaysia now ranks 10th among all export destinations for Japanese agricultural, forestry, fishery and food products, up from 13th place previously.
"This underscores Malaysia's growing importance as a key market for Japan in Southeast Asia and reflects the continued growth in demand for Japanese food products among Malaysian consumers and businesses," he said at the Japanese Cuisine Lecture Series organised by Jetro recently at Taylor's University.
He said awareness of washoku, or traditional Japanese cuisine — which is inscribed on the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2013 — has also boosted demand.
Takano noted that statistics from Japan's Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Ministry showed that the country's agricultural, forestry, fishery and food exports to Malaysia had reached 29.1 billion yen last year, a 26.3 per cent increase year-on-year compared with 2024.
He said e-commerce and demand generated from travel to Japan have also provided a platform to promote Japanese cuisine.
"The increase in Japanese restaurants globally demonstrates that Japanese cuisine has become well established internationally."
Across the Asean region, he said, Malaysia has strong potential as a gateway for the expansion of Japanese food culture and products.
"It is a multiracial, multicultural market that is well accustomed to diverse culinary traditions and international food offerings."
Takano outlined a successful Malaysian model that integrates human resource development, product innovation, halal readiness and efficient distribution networks that could serve as a valuable framework for promoting Japanese cuisine and food products across Asean and other Muslim-majority markets.
"The overall outlook remains positive and we expect more Japanese companies to establish food service businesses and operations in the coming years," he said.

Title: Round-the-clock Prasarana services for National Day
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: Prasarana will run 24-hour public transport services starting the night of Aug 30 this National Day.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the company was committed to supporting this year's celebrations in Putrajaya.
"We hope this will encourage more people to come to Putrajaya," he added after officiating at the Majlis Ekspresi Jalur Gemilang JAPEN@Petronas event in Pantai Dalam here.
Fahmi also confirmed that Malaysia Day celebrations would be held at the Borneo Cultural Centre in Kuching, Sarawak, describing its scale as comparable to Penang's PICCA Convention Centre, which hosted last year's event.
He said preparations were progressing well following last week's initial committee meeting, with the next planning session to take place on Aug 24.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said this year's Jalur Gemilang distribution features magnetic flags for vehicles.
"From motorists' feedback, they prefer magnets over those that are stuck onto the vehicle. So this is an improvement we've made this year."
He also called on RTM and other broadcasters to increase airplay for Faizal Tahir's Aku Berjanji, the official National Month theme song.

Title: 1,524 wild animal attacks since 2020, says Perhilitan
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The Wildlife and National Parks Department recorded 1,524 cases of human-wildlife conflict between 2020 and July this year.
Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the incidents resulted in 1,470 injuries and 54 deaths.
He attributed the conflicts to shrinking natural habitats, land clearing and development projects, leading to habitat fragmentation.
"These conditions force wildlife to seek new roaming areas near forests, plantations and neighbouring villages.
"In addition, members of the public who feed wildlife, particularly primates, encourage conflicts between humans and monkeys," he said, also citing poor waste management as a contributing factor.
Kadir said high breeding rates among primates had led to annual population growth as the species were highly adaptable with strong survival capabilities.
"Increased public awareness of wildlife conflict, and easier access to mass media and departmental complaint platforms have strengthened the government's ability to receive comprehensive reports from the public."
1:29 - In some cases, he said Perhilitan was moving away from complete reliance on costly catch-and-relocate methods and focusing on modern mitigation measures, including GPS satellite collars.
These are fitted on wild elephant herd leaders to monitor their movements in real time, triggering early warning systems when herds approach plantation or residential boundaries.
Kadir said patrol units also used thermal drones to safely detect wildlife, such as elephants or tigers, in dense brush before the animals entered villages.
"Camera traps, meanwhile, monitor intrusion hotspots to gather behavioural data for early control measures."
He urged the public to report any disturbances involving wildlife via the Perhilitan hotline at 1-800-88-5151 or its e-Aduan portal, and avoid taking matters into their own hands.

Title: Moderate earthquake hits southern Sumatra
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.3 on the Richter scale struck southern Sumatra, Indonesia at 11.15pm last night.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) in a statement said the earthquake was centred at coordinates six degrees South and 102.4 degrees East with a depth of 78km.
It is located 239km southwest of Pagar Alam, Indonesia,  according to the statement.
However, there is no tsunami threat to Malaysia.

Title: Pas ready to explain PN crisis complaint to RoS, says Takiyuddin
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas is ready to provide an explanation to the Registrar of Societies (RoS) if the regulator seeks clarification over a complaint concerning the crisis within Perikatan Nasional (PN), said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
He said it was the right of any party to lodge a complaint with the RoS, adding that it was up to the regulator to decide whether further action was warranted.
"Let the RoS make the decision. If the RoS asks us for an explanation, we will provide it," he told reporters in Pengkalan Chepa here tonight.
Takiyuddin, who is also PN secretary-general, said Pas was currently unaware of the nature of the complaint referred to by Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz.
"So far, we do not know what his complaint is," he said.
On cooperation within PN, Takiyuddin said component parties should use the coalition for the benefit of all its members.
He said Pas had never refused to allow Bersatu to use the PN logo, but the party had chosen to contest an election independently.
"We cannot force them, and we have never refused to give them the PN logo. But they chose not to accept it and that is up to them," he said.
Earlier,
Tun Faisal urged the RoS
to intervene in the ongoing PN crisis, alleging that Pas had taken unilateral actions that infringed on the rights of other component parties and contravened the PN Constitution.
Last Friday, PN chairman Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said Bersatu had automatically ceased to be a PN member after announcing plans to form a new coalition. Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali rejected the claim, saying there was no provision in the PN Constitution for automatic termination of a component party's membership.

Title: Pas to invite Umno leaders to annual muktamar
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas will invite Umno leaders to attend its 72nd muktamar in Kelantan next month.
Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the invitation letter would be sent soon.
"Following a meeting, we agreed to invite Umno leaders as our political partners.
"We will send an invitation letter to the Umno secretary-general (Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki), and it is up to the party to decide who will attend.
"Meanwhile, the party's wings, including the youth wing, will also invite their counterparts from Umno," he said when met after attending the Pas 72nd muktamar organising committee meeting here today.
He added that next month's muktamar would also mark Pas' 75th anniversary.
"We are still receiving motions from Pas divisions as some have yet to hold their meetings," he said.

Title: Tibetan activist's final act puts forgotten struggle in spotlight
Article:
NO one knew what Lobga Rang-zen was planning. Not the monk who was his friend of 30 years, not his niece in New York.
The niece was watching the World Cup on TV in Queens when she heard from a friend that her uncle had "burned himself" in front of the United Nations in Manhattan.
Tenzin Choekyi, 21, at first imagined a minor accident, but then came the details "and a wave of absolute terror hit me".
Rangzen, a longtime Tibetan activist aged 52, had set himself ablaze, and died.
The  incident barely registered in the US news, dominated that balmy July 2 night by the wedding of pop superstar Taylor Swift at Madison Square Garden on the other side of Manhattan.
But Rangzen's fellow exiled Tibetans, who have struggled to win international attention for their opposition to Chinese communist rule, greeted his passing with anguish and respect.
They erected a  shrine at the scene of his "self-immolation".
It has become a rallying point for Tibetan activists, below the turquoise-windowed facade of the United Nations.
"His passing has left many of us Tibetans with the fervour to act," said Jampa Choedup, a monk who had known Rangzen since 1997 and saw him the day before his death.
Rangzen was emulating the 170 monks and others who have set themselves on fire between 2009 and 2022 — mostly in China, but also in India and Nepal — in a last-resort protest after a bloody crackdown on mass demonstrations in Tibet in 2008.
Beijing, which considers Tibet an inalienable part of its territory, has only tightened its control since. On the eve of Rangzen's death, it adopted an "ethnic unity" law that critics say will further degrade minority rights.
Rangzen's livestream of his death shows a heavy-set man striding across a street in a traditional "chuba" robe and planting a Tibetan flag outside the UN.
He then erupts in flames twice his height, dark smoke billowing. Too late, a UN security guard rushes in with a fire extinguisher.
Rangzen was pronounced dead about an hour later in hospital.
He was the first Tibetan to self-immolate in the United States, which is home to about 25,000 Tibetans — overwhelmingly followers of Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, who fled Tibet in 1959 and lives in India.
The niece Choekyi remembered Rangzen as a "joyful" man who loved joining weekly Tibetan "gorshey" circle dances.
Choedup, the monk, said the day before Rangzen died, he talked about Tibetans' individual responsibility to seek freedom.
His real name was Lobsang Palden. He fled Tibet as a young man and spent 14 years as a monk in southern India, then moved to the US in 2006, settling in Queens.
He adopted the name "Rang-zen" which means "independence" — echoing his desire for an independent Tibet.
He was not fluent in English and drifted between jobs before becoming an Uber driver.
According to Ugen and Choe-dup, one of his uncles died in combat and another in prison after his capture while fighting for Chushi Gangdruk, an anti-China guerilla force established with CIA support in 1958.
As China cemented its seven-decade grip over the Tibetan plateau and abandoned negotiations on Tibet's future with the Dalai Lama, some of his followers resorted to self-sacrifice, leaving the Nobel peace laureate in a bind about how to react.
Beijing, which contends it has improved economic and social conditions in Tibet, accused the Dalai Lama of "glorifying" self-immolations.
After Rangzen's death, the head of the Tibetan government-in-exile, Penpa Tsering, urged all Tibetans to "cherish" their lives.
"While we honour his devotion, human life is precious and must be preserved to serve the long-term struggle for Tibet," Tsering said in a statement.
In his video, Rangzen criticised Chinese policies and urged exiled Tibetans to help build a new future. "There is no need to mourn for me," he said.
* The writer is from  AFP

Title: Five bodies hanging from bridge revive Mexico town's drug war fears
Article:
POZOS DE GAMBOA, Mexico: Horrific drug violence plagued the Mexican state of Zacatecas for years, until relative calm set in. Then one morning in July this small town woke up to find five bodies dangling from a bridge – a grim calling card that showed the bloodshed never really left.
These days in Pozos de Gamboa, a Zacatecas town of 5,000 that is known for growing beans, people are terrified. No one goes out after dark and no one talks about that morning when the bodies showed up.
Zacatecas is key to the drug trade because it links central Mexico with the north and west of the country and features routes that are key to smuggling cocaine and drugs north to the hungry consumer market in the United States.
The state of 1.6 million people had become painfully used to narcotics-related violence as rival gangs fought each other, with bodies turning up almost on a daily basis and people going missing right and left.
Then things calmed down, a lot. Killings in Zacatecas fell from around 1,300 in 2022 to 144 in 2025, according to government figures. The government has attributed the decline to better coordination between state and federal law enforcement officials.
The calm spell ended shockingly on July 18 with the spectacle of the bodies hanging from the bridge. The victims included a former mayor, civil servants and business people from other parts of the state. Five other bodies were found elsewhere in town that same day.
Mexico's two largest drug cartels – Jalisco New Generation and  Sinaloa – have been fighting to control Zacatecas because of its strategic value in the US-bound drug trade.
- 'THEY KILL OVER NOTHING' -
Prosecutors opened a probe into the killings and the state government promised "an immediate and forceful response," while noting that violence like this had been on the decline. It asked for help from the army and the National Guard to boost security in Zacatecas.
AFP visited Pozos de Gamboa and observed that on the road here from the state capital, also called Zacatecas, there were no roadblocks and just a few police patrol cars out and about.
One Pozos de Gamboa resident who declined to be named, fearing for his safety, described it as being like a ghost town – "as if no one ever lived here."
"Here, you always used to see people," this man said. But now, "at 9 in the evening there is no one out on the street."
Indeed, in this town most people have lost a relative or an acquaintance – dead or missing – to all the drug violence.
When people go missing they are routinely killed, this man said. "They make it so the bodies do not smell."
"They killed a brother of ours," he added. "They kill over nothing at all."
The bridge where the bodies were found last month had been used in the past as a spot for the drug cartels to leave these grim messages.
A woman who runs a food stall in the street said she saw the bodies hanging as early 4 am.
The image recalled the worst years of Mexico's drug wars, when the government deployed federal forces in 2006 to fight the cartels and these crime gangs fought back, hanging bodies from bridges or dumping them elsewhere in public to intimidate rivals and the security forces.
The Pozos de Gamboa killings drew the attention of leftist President Claudia Sheinbaum's government, which promised to arrest whoever was behind them.
She has deployed soldiers in violence-plagued states such as Sinaloa and Michoacan as she endures pressure from US President Donald Trump to intervene directly in Mexico against the cartels so as to keep drugs from crossing the border into the United States.--AFP

Title: The Iran war has exposed the world's energy vulnerability
Article:
THE lasting legacy of the Iran war will likely be a renewed impetus for energy-importing nations to lessen their dependence on fossil fuels.
The big question for these countries is how to accomplish this in a cost-effective, politically acceptable way that does not create new vulnerabilities.
This is no easy feat. The debate is often framed along left- and right-wing political fault lines.
Progressives typically say the conflict underscores the need to accelerate the transition to renewables and electric vehicles (EVs), while conservatives argue it shows the need to develop more fossil fuel production outside the Middle East.
The Iran war, launched by the US and Israel on Feb 28, has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.
The narrow waterway previously carried close to 20 per cent of global crude, refined products and liquefied natural gas (LNG).
For fuel-importing nations, the Iran war is the second crisis in four years.
Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine caused prices of crude, fuel, LNG and thermal coal to spike globally amid fears that exports from Russia would be curtailed. The status quo is clearly no longer acceptable, so the question is how energy security can be achieved moving forward.
Australia,  the world's leading diesel importer, offers a prime example of the dilemma facing fuel importers.
The answer is complex and offers some far-reaching lessons. Australia relies on imports for about 80 per cent of its liquid fuel needs.
Its eight refineries operating at the start of the century have been reduced to just two — with processing capacities of just over 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) each.
The country imported about 861,000 bpd of light and middle distillates in 2025, with diesel accounting for about 60 per cent of that.
The threat of ongoing supply disruptions and sharply higher prices led Australia's government to recently announce an A$4 million pre-feasibility study for a new oil refinery.
If built, it would be the first such plant in 60 years. The basic plan is to build a plant in Western Australia to supply  the mining and agricultural sectors.
The state, which is nearly five times the size of France but home to just three million people, imports around 200,000 bpd of light and middle distillates, according to Kpler.
The new refinery was proposed by fertiliser and urea maker Perdaman, which has described the plant as a "game changer for Australian fuel security".
But the question is who would pay for it. A modern, economically viable refinery requires a capacity of at least 300,000 bpd.
A similar-sized plant being built in Ghana is estimated to cost around US$12 billion, and would likely cost substantially more in Australia given higher labour and land charges.
Would it instead be better to encourage mining companies and farmers to electrify their operations?
Fortescue Metals Group is doing just that and Australia's third-biggest iron ore miner says this  is already paying dividends.
Data shows that Fortescue's adoption of electric mining vehicles and renewable electricity generation provides a net annual benefit of A$1.2 billion  over using diesel and natural gas power generation.
It's not just miners and farmers that may benefit from going electric.
Sales of EVs more than tripled in July from the same month a year earlier, while plug-in hybrids surged 157 per cent and mild hybrids jumped 206 per cent, suggesting consumers are responding to fuel-security concerns.
It may sound like a contradiction, but it's possible that Australia could benefit from pursuing both paths to some degree.
There are signs that this process is already underway.
For example, Vietnam is adopting policies to boost the domestic production and sales of EVs, but also electric scooters, a major shift given motorcycles are the most popular form of personal transport in this nation of 102 million people.
Similarly, Indonesia is targeting an all-electric bus fleet by 2045, while also promoting a shift to electric scooters and EVs.
Thailand is providing a subsidy of up to 100,000 baht (US$3,020) for purchases of EVs as it is rapidly building public charging infrastructure.
The answer to energy security will vary by nation, but the common theme is the need for diversification — both in where countries source their energy and the types they consume.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: NST Leader: Malaysia must first answer how many migrant workers it needs
Article:
MANAGING migrant workers has been an issue for policymakers for the  longest time. Although numerous measures have been adopted by the government, it remains a problem in search of a solution.
Tenaganita, a labour rights organisation,  suggests  that regularising existing  migrant workers  might be the solution rather than importing more from overseas. But first, how many migrant workers are there in the country?
There aren't reliable figures available, especially for undocumented workers. According to the Human Resources Ministry, there were 2.1 million documented workers as of June last year. The majority are from Bangladesh, followed by Indonesia and Nepal. Other countries that supply labour are Myanmar, India, Pakistan, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, China, Laos, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. This is the latest data announced by the government.
As for undocumented workers, we enter a dark terrain. Even estimates vary by a couple of millions. One estimate puts the number of such workers at 3.1 million, though some analysts say it might include foreign students.
More accurate would be the World Bank's 2020 report, which puts the number of irregular workers between 1.23 million and 1.46 million. But the figures are five years too old.
According to the  Statistics Department, there are 3.38 million in what it terms as "non-citizens" in the country. Again, this is  a different classification. What Malaysia needs is a first good step, that is,  to get all agencies to speak with one figure and one language.
Tenaganita's proposal has pros and cons but it deserves consideration.  Malaysia relies heavily  on foreign labour, and the proposal  highlights a glaring inefficiency in how the country manages the workers it already has.
If workers can move to sectors where labour is genuinely needed, everyone potentially benefits: employers will fill vacancies faster, workers remain employed, and the government reduces the cost and administrative burden of fresh recruitment.
However, there is a risk of creating a permanent migrant-dependent  workforce. Easier redeployment could reduce employers' incentive  to automate, improve wages or attract Malaysians to these sectors. There are also potential displacement concerns.
Labour unions may argue that readily available migrant workers could suppress wage growth or reduce incentives to hire locals, particularly in lower-skilled occupations. Enforcement challenges are also possible.
Without effective monitoring, labour policy could inadvertently increase undocumented employment. The proposal also comes against the backdrop of Malaysia's ambition to become a high-income high-productivity economy.
A nation cannot indefinitely compete by importing ever more low-cost labour while lamenting stagnant productivity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aruz, Ferrari drivers call truce, but police probe rolls on
Article:
NILAI: The two drivers involved in a fight at Kilometre 276 of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) southbound here yesterday are said to have reached an amicable settlement.
Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said, however, that police would continue investigating the incident, which occurred
around 11am yesterday
.
"The latest development involves the 40-year-old Ferrari driver and 35-year-old Perodua Aruz driver in the incident that went viral on social media.
"Both parties met and held private discussions at their own request, without the involvement or intervention of police," he said in a statement today.
Johari said the discussions resulted in both parties reaching a mutual agreement to resolve the dispute amicably and not pursue the matter further.
"Both parties also agreed, at their own request, to issue a joint media statement to explain the resolution reached following the video of the incident going viral on social media," he said.
Johari said despite the amicable settlement, it would not affect the police investigation.
"The investigation will continue and be completed based on the statements and evidence obtained for further action.
"Both individuals have been released on police bail, with each released under the guarantee of one guarantor," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Duit kutu': RM1.7mil losses, 35 reports lodged
Article:
JITRA: Police have received 35 reports involving a woman linked to duit kutu (informal money pool), with total losses amounting to RM1.7 million.
Kubang Pasu district police chief superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the reports were lodged by victims aged between 23 and 53.
He said investigations were being conducted under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
Earlier, it was reported that three family members were missing after leaving their home in Taman Desa Bayanmas, Bukit Kayu Hitam, on July 20.
Following this, the woman's 62-year-old father lodged a police report at the Bukit Kayu Hitam police station last Monday after failing to trace his daughter, son-in-law and grandchild.
However, the couple
surrendered
themselves at the Kubang Pasu district police headquarters at 1.50am last Thursday and were remanded for four days, which ended today.
The
remand
period for the husband and wife, aged 39 and 36, has been extended by two more days from today to assist in investigations into the kutu debts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 60,000 illicit cigarettes seized in Kota Baru, Vellfire driver arrested
Article:
KOTA BARU: The General Operations Force (GOF) seized 60,000 cigarettes suspected to be duty-unpaid, valued at RM112,200, and arrested a 37-year-old driver after intercepting a Toyota Vellfire at the shoulder of the Pasir Tumboh Bridge early this morning.
Southeast Brigade GOF Commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the suspect was stopped during
Op Taring Wawasan Kelantan
at about 1.30am after he failed to produce relevant documentation for the goods and tested positive for drugs.
In a statement, he said other items seized included the Toyota Vellfire valued at RM95,000, two mobile phones worth RM3,000 and RM250 in cash, bringing the total value of the seizure to RM210,450. The case is being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967.
Radzi said the suspect and all seized items were handed over to the Criminal zInvestigation Department and Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department of the Kota Baru district police Headquarters.
He said initial investigations found that the suspect had worked as a full-time driver for the past three years and was paid RM200 for each delivery, adding that the GOF would continue to intensify monitoring and patrols within its area of responsibility in Kota Baru to curb smuggling activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah to acquire 30pct stake in 2 new oil and gas fields, says Hajiji
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government will acquire a 30 per cent stake in two new oil and gas fields off the state's east coast, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the state government was also finalising the acquisition of a 40 per cent equity stake in a floating liquefied natural gas (LNG) facility project in Sabah.
"The agreement for this partnership will be signed soon. The government will also develop new industrial parks, including in Kota Belud, and a blue economy hub in Kudat to further boost investment in the state and increase domestic economic activity," he said at Upko's 32nd anniversary celebration and the opening of the party's 17th Triennial Conference here today.
Hajiji, who is also Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman, said the development was part of the Sabah government's efforts to strengthen its participation in the oil and gas industry through strategic collaboration with Petronas under the Commercial Collaborative Agreement.
He said the collaboration had increased the state government's equity holding in the exploration and development of Sabah's oil and gas industry, while also creating opportunities for local companies to participate in the sector.
Hajiji said the state government continued to focus on strengthening its financial performance and increasing revenue collection as an important foundation for Sabah's development.
He said the state had maintained annual revenue collection at about RM7 billion since 2022 and expected it to increase to RM8 billion this year.
"In 2025 alone, RM7.6 billion in investment value in the manufacturing sector was recorded, almost 208 per cent against 2024," he said.
He said the achievement was also supported by Sabah's economic resilience in facing various domestic and global challenges, further strengthening its position as a strategic investment destination.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MOH adds boat services to improve healthcare access for Orang Asli in Hulu Perak
Article:
IPOH: The Health Ministry (MOH) has introduced additional boat services to strengthen healthcare access in Hulu Perak, reducing emergency response times for Orang Asli residents in the Kemar Resettlement Scheme (RPS) in Gerik.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the RM350,000 Medic Boat 8 was vital for more than 4,500 Orang Asli residents in the area, who depend entirely on waterways as their main means of access and transport.
"The 12-passenger multipurpose boat will add to the MOH's existing fleet of six boats. However sophisticated government assets may be, they are of little value without the dedication of our personnel on the ground," he said in a Facebook post.
Earlier, he launched the Medic Boat 8 service at the Belum Rainforest Resort jetty as part of his working visit to Hulu Perak.
He also thanked healthcare workers, including doctors, nurses and boat operators, for their continued readiness to brave river currents and adverse weather conditions in carrying out their duty to treat patients.
"Our principle under Malaysia Madani is clear: healthcare must be accessible to all. The challenging terrain and remote geography of the interior will never be allowed to stand in the way of access to the best possible care," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah to channel RM1.5bil interim payment into infrastructure, welfare
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Sabah government will use the increased interim payment from Putrajaya to improve infrastructure and strengthen welfare initiatives for the people, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the Sabah government had accepted an interim arrangement under which the payment, previously set at RM26 million, had been increased to RM1.5 billion from this year.
"We welcome the prime minister's decision to increase the interim payment, and we will use these funds to build more paved roads in Sabah, construct concrete bridges and improve water and electricity supplies.
"It will also implement development and welfare initiatives for the people of Sabah, such as building more Rumah SMJ houses and expanding the Sentuhan Kasih Rakyat (Syukur) programme.
"In short, whatever we receive from the Federal Government will be channelled back to the people in various forms of incentives and assistance," he said when speaking at Upko's 32nd Anniversary Celebration and 17th Triennial Delegates Conference at Hongkod Koisaan Hall in Penampang near here.
On Sabah's 40 per cent entitlement to federal revenue derived from the state, Hajiji said the government would continue to pursue its right, as enshrined in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), through government-to-government negotiations with the Federal Government.
He said the entitlement was Sabah's most significant right under MA63 and was provided for under Articles 112C and 112D of the Federal Constitution.
Hajiji said the Sabah government's position would continue to be conveyed to the Federal Government, including at the MA63 Technical Committee meeting in Putrajaya on Aug 3, which was also attended by Ewon Benedick in his capacity as deputy chief minister.
To date, 13 claims related to MA63 have been implemented, including the regulation of energy, deep-sea fishing licensing and regulation, recognition of the Public Works Department and Department of Irrigation and Drainage under Treasury Instruction 182, administration of the judiciary in Sabah, administration of Sipadan and Ligitan islands, labour and the environment.
Meanwhile, Hajiji said the Sabah government continued to place strong emphasis on financial performance and increasing revenue collection, with annual revenue maintained at RM7 billion since 2022 and expected to rise to RM8 billion this year.
He said the Sabah government had also strengthened the state's economic resilience despite various domestic and global challenges, positioning Sabah as a strategic investment destination.
"In 2025 alone, RM7.6 billion in investments in the manufacturing sector was recorded, representing an increase of nearly 208 per cent compared with 2024," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Strong winds fuel Bromo wildfire, blaze spreads to 520ha
Article:
JAKARTA: The Mount Bromo wildfire has surged out of control, spreading across 520 hectares as strong winds fanned flames from the slopes into the savanna of East Java, authorities confirmed Sunday.
Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park (TNBTS) Authority head Rudijanta Tjahja Nugraha said the blaze flared up again on Saturday night, burning not only the slopes but also the savanna.
"The fire grew larger due to fairly strong winds since yesterday afternoon, allowing it to spread rapidly from the upper slopes towards the lower areas," he said, according to Antara News Agency.
He added that with grass and vegetation already dry, the area was highly susceptible to burning.
The TNBTS Authority has closed Mount Bromo to tourists at all entrances from 10pm Saturday until further notice to facilitate firefighting efforts and ensure visitor safety. Visitors were offered options to reschedule bookings or receive refunds.
Meanwhile, Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said the investigation into the cause of the wildfire has been left to law enforcement authorities.
"Anyone who carries out forest and land burning will receive the appropriate punishment," he said, as quoted by Antara.
The TNBTS Authority earlier said the fire was suspected to have been caused by human activity.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thai school shooting: Students, teachers mourn 12-year-old victim
Article:
BANGKOK: Dozens of bereaved students, parents and teachers queued at a Buddhist temple in Thailand on Sunday to pray over the body of a 12-year-old girl, one of eight victims of a home and school shooting two days earlier.
The 14-year-old assailant shot dead the grandparents who raised him at their home north of Bangkok on Friday before killing six others at his school, using his grandfather's handgun, and then turning the gun on himself, authorities said.
Investigators are still seeking a motive, but police said on Sunday the boy had watched violent videos online and once brought a BB gun to school. Officials said earlier he faced academic-related stress and a classmate said he was bullied.
Mourners dressed in black gathered on Sunday in the pavilion of Wat Lat Pla Duk in Nonthaburi province, bordering Bangkok, where the body of the slain schoolgirl, Naphat Chaima, lay for a ceremonial bath.
She died in hospital on Saturday after suffering gunshot wounds at the school, police said. Five teachers and school staff were also killed on Friday.
Mourners took turns gently pouring water over a hand of the deceased while others lit incense sticks and folded their hands in prayer.
"She was a good kid. A kid who loved to do every activity," said the girl's music teacher, who declined to give her name.
"She loved to dance."
Several psychologists were available to consult with grieving children under the care of their parents, an AFP journalist saw.
Another woman said her 12-year-old daughter was a classmate of the dead girl. They had done cheerleading together.
"This family lost their daughter. I came to support the mother" who lost her child too soon, she told AFP.
She said she wanted the school to tighten security, questioning how the teenage shooter could have brought a gun and bullets into the school.
However, ultimately the incident was "beyond anyone's control", she said.
Her daughter was able to exit a school building, physically unharmed, through a back door, she said.
- 'REAL CAUSE' -
Investigators have interviewed 17 witnesses and were examining the boy's computer and phone to determine the "real cause of the shooting", Atthapol Anusit, a deputy police commander for the region surrounding the capital, told reporters earlier.
"We looked into his PC and found history that he watched violent videos on social media," Atthapol said.
"From questioning the kids, we know that he brought a BB gun to school last year but a teacher seized it."
Witnesses told police the boy had been interested in guns for a year or two, Atthapol said, adding that he had learned how to use one by watching content on social media.
The child had lived with his grandparents since he was two years old after his parents had separated, he said.
The boy's father apologised "to society for what my son did" on Friday, according to local media.
Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has said the boy experienced school-related stress, and his dead grandmother was a former teacher who had been "quite strict on him about studying."
Thailand has one of the highest rates of gun ownership in the region, with around 10 million firearms estimated to be in circulation – roughly one for every seven inhabitants.
Officials have promised stricter gun laws since Friday's shooting, but previous pledges have failed to prevent repeated shootings.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alleged cartel boss Kinahan extradited from UAE to Ireland
Article:
DUBAI: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates handed over alleged transnational cartel boss Daniel Kinahan to face trial in Ireland, the Gulf country's official media reported on Sunday.
The 49-year-old Irishman allegedly ran a group out of Dubai that has been linked by US and European authorities to a vast criminal enterprise dealing in drug smuggling and money laundering.
The report published by the Emirates News Agency said justice ministers from the Gulf state and Ireland discussed Kinahan's extradition during a recent phone call.
Kinahan "was extradited by the UAE to the Irish authorities at their formal request to face prosecution for offences related to transnational organised crime, including allegations of leading a criminal organisation, murder and illicit drug trafficking," said the report.
Kinahan was arrested in Dubai in April after a warrant was issued in Ireland for "alleged serious organised crime offences" and lost appeals against extradition.
Irish national broadcaster RTE reported his extradition flight had departed the UAE earlier Sunday but did not specify what time it was due to land at Casement Aerodrome in Baldonnel.
On arrival in Ireland, Kinahan was expected to be taken to the Special Crime Court in Dublin amid a large security operation, according to an earlier RTE report.
The transnational group, known as the Kinahan Organised Crime Group (KOCG), is alleged to be the most powerful criminal organisation in Ireland with wealth estimated by Irish police at over 1 billion euros (£856 million).
Kinahan would be the second senior figure in the cartel to be extradited from Dubai.
Sean McGovern, described by a judge as "senior lieutenant in the cartel", was the first senior associate to be extradited after his arrest in 2024.
In June, he was sentenced to 24 years in prison in Ireland after pleading guilty to directing organised crime and attempted murder.
The case related to a long-running violent feud between the Kinahan cartel and the rival Dublin-based Hutch gang.
The US government in 2022 imposed sanctions on Kinahan and other members of his family identified as leaders of the cartel.
It designated them as running a narcotics trafficking organisation active in Ireland, the United Kingdom and throughout mainland Europe, and engaging in "money laundering, firearms trafficking, and murder."
The US Treasury said Kinahan was believed to run the cartel's day-to-day operations, while his brother Christopher was also designated.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Air India pilot flagged for confirmatory drug test after 300ft plunge
Article:
MUMBAI: India's aviation ministry said Sunday that an Air India pilot whose flight plunged dramatically in turbulence injuring 17 passengers and crew is undergoing a "confirmatory" psychoactive drug test.
The Airbus A320, carrying 137 passengers and eight crew, lost around 300 feet (91 metres) on August 4 while flying from Phuket in Thailand to New Delhi, before stabilising and landing safely, the civil aviation ministry said.
Eight passengers and four cabin crew members were admitted to hospitals after landing in the Indian capital, whose conditions were described as "stable", after which both pilots were given a standard "psychoactive substance screening test", the statement read.
"The screening test in respect of the Pilot-in-Command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing," it said.
"Samples have accordingly been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited."
The ministry said the flight has been classified as a "Serious Incident", and that India's Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has launched an investigation.
Both pilots have been removed from the flying roster pending outcomes of investigation.
"Further action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results," it added.
Videos of the incident's aftermath showed cabin baggage strewn across the aisle. Some of those injured were taken to hospital on stretchers.
Air India, in a statement earlier on Sunday, confirmed that a "post-flight screening test" had been conducted on the flight's pilots, but it said the results had not been shared with the company.
The incident is the latest in a series of setbacks for the Indian carrier, which appointed a new executive on Wednesday.
Since taking over Air India in 2022, India's Tata Group has embarked on an ambitious overhaul, ordering hundreds of aircraft and upgrading its ageing fleet.
While the airline has managed to modernise operations and integrate the group's aviation businesses, it has faced persistent headwinds including aircraft delivery delays and airspace closures caused by the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict.
But the biggest blow to the airline's image came in June 2025, when Air India Flight 171 – a London-bound Boeing 787 Dreamliner – crashed shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad, killing all but one of the 242 people on board and 19 people on the ground.
The carrier has now turned to former Ethiopian Airlines chief Tewolde Gebremariam, widely seen as an industry veteran capable of righting the ship, as its new CEO as it seeks to execute a turnaround.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Upko's entry strengthens Sabah political stability, says Hajiji
Article:
PENAMPANG: Upko's entry into Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) will further strengthen political stability in Sabah, said GRS chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the party, led by its president Datuk Ewon Benedick, would also enhance cooperation among local parties in efforts to develop Sabah.
"In fact, when we received Upko's application to join GRS, we saw it as a positive development in Sabah politics and welcomed it with an open heart.
"With political stability assured, it will certainly be easier for the Sabah government to focus on the people's development agenda, the state's economic prosperity and infrastructure development," he said when speaking at Upko's 32nd Anniversary Celebration and 17th Triennial Delegates Conference at Hongkod Koisaan Hall, KDCA, here.
He said that as partners in GRS, the component parties might come from different backgrounds and have different foundations in their respective struggles, but they were all under the same roof and fighting for the same land of Sabah.
Hajiji, who is also Sabah Chief Minister, said he greatly appreciated the strong support extended by Ewon and Upko members throughout his tenure, which had enabled him to lead Sabah's development through the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) 1.0 development plan, now continued under SMJ 2.0.
He said Ewon's appointment as one of the three Deputy Chief Ministers, as well as Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, carried a major responsibility to ensure Sabah's investment, industrial development and entrepreneurship agendas were successfully realised in line with the objectives of SMJ 2.0.
Hajiji said strong political unity and close cooperation were key to a more developed, successful and prosperous future for Sabah.
"This is the agenda that we must implement so that future generations of Sabahans can be proud of the legacy that we will leave behind for them," he said.
Also present were Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) acting president Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) president Datuk Chin Su Phin, and Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah (Harapan) president Tan Sri Liew Yun Fah.
GRS comprises Parti Gagasan Rakyat, Parti Cinta Sabah, LDP, PBS, Harapan and Upko.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Syria, Russia reach deal to turn military bases into training centres
Article:
DAMASCUS: Syria said on Sunday that it reached a deal with Moscow on the fate of Russia's two bases in the country, which it once used to provide military support to ousted leader Bashar al-Assad during the Syrian civil war.
Syria's official SANA news agency quoted the foreign ministry as saying that Hmeimim airbase and Tartus naval base, Russia's only two official military bases outside the former Soviet Union, would be turned into "joint training and capacity-building centres, within new arrangements that preserve mutual interests."
The memorandum of understanding, which followed a year and a half of negotiations, "set a time limit of no more than three months to complete the process", SANA added.
In the meantime, civilian facilities at both bases will be handed over to Damascus.
Russia was a key Assad ally during Syria's 13-year conflict, and provided vital military support that kept the former leader's forces in power.
Assad's ouster in 2024 dealt a major blow to Moscow's influence in the region, and President Vladimir Putin has been working to build relations with the new authorities in Damascus to secure the future of the bases.
Both the Hmeimim and Tartus bases had remained operational while talks were ongoing.
Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani visited the sites on Sunday "to inspect the facilities and installations included in the historic memorandum of understanding", according to SANA.
Syria has expressed a willingness to cooperate with Moscow, and President Ahmed al-Sharaa has been received by Putin in Moscow twice since taking over.
Damascus, however, has repeatedly demanded that Russia extradite Assad, who has been sheltering in Moscow with his wife since his ouster.
Earlier this year, the Kremlin withdrew its forces from the Qamishli airport in Syria's northeast.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Final LMSB2 vessel Tunku Osman Jewa launched in Turkiye
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The navy's third Littoral Mission Ship Batch 2 (LMSB2) vessel has been named Tunku Osman Jewa and launched at Istanbul Shipyard, Turkiye, today.
The vessel, bearing pennant number 143, is the final ship in the three-vessel LMSB2 series built at the shipyard and is expected to be delivered to the navy by the end of next year.
In a social media post, the RMN said the naming and launching ceremony was witnessed by the Sultan of Kedah, Al Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Ibni Almarhum Sultan Badlishah, and officiated by the Sultanah of Kedah, Sultanah Maliha binti Almarhum Tengku Ariff, as the Royal Sponsor.
The vessel was named in honour of the late General Tan Sri Tunku Osman Tunku Mohammad Jewa, a Kedah royal family member who was the first armed forces chief appointed from among Malaysians.
The Defence Ministry delegation was led by armed forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.
Also present were ministry's deputy secretary-general (Management) Datin Roszanina Wahab and deputy navy chief vice-admiral Datuk Badarudin Taha.
The launch completes the LMSB2 series at Istanbul Shipyard, following Tunku Laksamana Abdul Jalil (141) and Raja Laut (142).
The Tunku-class vessel, based on the Ada-class corvette design by Turkish defence firm Savunma Teknolojileri Mühendislik (STM), measures 99.56m in length and 14.42m in width, and is designed for multi-dimensional naval operations.
All three vessels will now undergo sensor system integration, installation of warfare systems and weapons, followed by harbour acceptance trials and sea acceptance trials.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gaza death toll rises to 73,386 amid ongoing Israeli aggression
Article:
GAZA: Health authorities reported on Sunday that the death toll from Israel's ongoing aggression on the Gaza Strip has risen to 73,386, with 174,250 others injured, since Oct 7, 2023, the Palestine News and Info Agency (WAFA) reported.
Hospitals across the enclave confirmed that they received two fatalities over the past 24 hours, including one person who succumbed to wounds sustained earlier, as well as eight injured people.
They said the death toll since the ceasefire took effect on Oct 11, 2025, has reached 1,258, while the number of injuries has risen to 4,139.
The number of bodies recovered from under the rubble since then has reached 807.
Meanwhile, a number of victims remain trapped under the rubble and on the roads, as ambulance and rescue teams remain unable to reach them, the authorities said.
– Bernama-Wafa
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: If police stop you in Malaysia, here's what you should know
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 10 — It happens more often than many people realise.
Maybe you’re pulled over at a roadblock. Maybe police stop you during an operation at a shopping mall or perhaps an officer approaches you on the street asking a few questions.
Or you maybe one of the rare ones who’ve had a knock on your door.
Do you have to answer everything? Can they search your phone? What if they ask you to follow them to the police station?
Then there’s the famous line we’ve all heard in countless Hollywood movies:
“I want my lawyer!” Does that actually work in Malaysia?
We’ve all seen the scenes.
A suspect is arrested, turns to the officer and declares:
“I want my lawyer.”
Questioning stops. A lawyer appears moments later.
In Malaysia, it doesn’t quite happen like that.
If you’ve been arrested, you have the right to consult a lawyer and to contact a family member or trusted friend.
Police should generally give you a reasonable opportunity to speak to your lawyer, although there are limited circumstances where they may delay this if immediate questioning is necessary for the investigation.
You should also tell your family or lawyer where you were arrested, why you were arrested and which police station you’re being taken to.
However before any of that happens, most encounters with police start much more simply.
Can police check your phone?
For many Malaysians, this is probably the first question that comes to mind.
The Malaysian Bar’s latest Red Book says police may inspect your mobile phone if they have a lawful reason to do so, such as when they reasonably suspect you’ve committed an offence, you’re being investigated, or you’ve been arrested.
If an officer asks to inspect your phone, don’t panic—but don’t be afraid to ask questions either.
Politely ask why your phone is being inspected and whether you’re being investigated or suspected of committing an offence.
Understanding why police are exercising that power can help you better understand your rights throughout the interaction.
A police officer stops you. What’s the first thing you should do?
First, stay calm.
If the officer is in uniform, make a mental note of their name and identification number. If they’re using a patrol car or motorcycle, note the vehicle registration number if you can.
If they’re not in uniform, politely ask to see their police authority card.
The colour tells you what authority they have:
Blue — Inspector and above.
Yellow — Officers below the rank of Inspector.
White — Reserve police.
Red — Suspended police officer with no police powers.
If possible, remember the officer’s name and identification number before the conversation continues.
Before answering questions, ask one yourself
People often assume that if police are questioning them, they’re already under arrest.
That’s not necessarily true.
Instead, politely ask:
“Am I under arrest?”
It might be the most important question you ask.
If the answer is no, you’re generally free to leave and do not have to accompany the police to a station simply because they ask.
If you’re told yes, or if you are handcuffed or prevented from leaving, you’re considered under arrest.
What information must you actually provide?
If you’ve simply been stopped by police, you’re generally only required to provide your personal particulars: Your name; NRIC number; and address.
Beyond that, your rights depend on the circumstances.
The guide also makes clear that police cannot arrest someone simply because they want that person to give a witness statement.
If you’re under arrest, ask these two questions
If police tell you you’re under arrest, don’t argue or physically resist.
Instead, ask:
“Why am I under arrest?”
Police should inform you why you’re being arrested.
Then ask:
“Which police station are you taking me to?”
Knowing where you’re being taken allows you to inform your lawyer or family member as soon as you’re able.
Can police search your car?
Yes, they can.
The updated Red Book explains that police have powers to stop and search vehicles in certain circumstances.
If your vehicle is being searched, remain cooperative but ask why the search is being conducted and whether you’re being investigated or suspected of committing an offence.
As with any interaction, note the officer’s name, rank and, if possible, the police vehicle’s registration number.
Can they search your pockets or bag?
Police may conduct searches during certain operations, but there’s a practical tip many people don’t know.
Instead of allowing officers to reach into your pockets or bag themselves, remove the contents yourself one item at a time, identify each item aloud and then turn your pockets or bag inside out.
If you’re a woman, any body search must be conducted by a female officer.
Strip searches aren’t automatic
Television often gives the impression that every arrest ends with a strip search.
It doesn’t.
The Red Book explains there are different types of body searches, ranging from a simple pat-down to strip, intimate and intrusive searches.
The more invasive the search, the higher the level of authorisation required.
How long can police keep you?
Police may generally detain someone for up to 24 hours while investigations are carried out.
If investigators need more time, they must bring you before a magistrate to apply for a remand order.
The magistrate isn’t obliged to grant the full period requested and may refuse the application or approve a shorter remand instead.
If you appear before a magistrate, tell the court if you’ve been denied access to a lawyer, require medical treatment or have been mistreated while in custody.
Before you sign anything… slow down
Whether it’s a witness statement or another document, don’t rush.
Read every page carefully.
Make sure it accurately reflects what you said.
If something is wrong, ask for it to be corrected before signing, and sign immediately below the last sentence so nothing can be added afterwards.
The bottom line
Most encounters with police end without incident.
Knowing your rights isn’t about refusing to cooperate or making an officer’s job harder. It’s about understanding what police can legally do, what you’re legally required to do, and asking the right questions if you’re ever stopped, questioned or arrested.

which explains the rights and responsibilities of the public during interactions with police.
