Title: Pulau Tuba’s authentic village life pitched as Langkawi’s next big tourism secret
Article:
LANGKAWI, Aug 10 — Pulau Tuba has the potential to attract more domestic and international tourists with its authentic traditional village atmosphere and unique cultural experiences, said Kedah Tourism, Culture and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Salleh Saidin.
He said despite Langkawi recording more than three million tourist arrivals, visitor numbers to Pulau Tuba remained relatively low, highlighting the island’s untapped potential as a “hidden gem”.
“Tourist arrivals in Langkawi reach the millions, yet only a small number visit Pulau Tuba. This shows the island has tremendous potential that has yet to be fully developed.
“It offers a sense of tranquillity and an atmosphere that is difficult to find elsewhere. The local community continues to preserve its heritage and traditional cultural values, complemented by an authentic village landscape, including buffaloes roaming freely,” he told reporters.
Mohd Salleh said visitors could also sample unique local seafood delicacies such as bronok (sea cucumber) and siput gayam, a type of shellfish associated with the island.
“Tourists today are no longer simply looking for luxurious buildings and facilities, they are seeking unique experiences. I am confident that Pulau Tuba has the potential to become a premier tourism destination, and we will focus on promoting its unique attractions to international visitors.
“The state government recognises Pulau Tuba’s special appeal, so we will not neglect it. Greater focus and attention will be given to the island,” he said.
He added that various programmes and events were being organised to attract visitors to Pulau Tuba, which would help boost the local tourism sector and generate economic benefits for the community.
Meanwhile, 31 media practitioners from Kedah were given the opportunity to experience the island’s unique lifestyle, culture, traditional cuisine, and local activities.
They also participated in traditional games such as menarik upih (areca frond racing) and sampled local specialities, including buffalo curry.
Pulau Tuba has a population of about 5,000 and is one of the 99 islands that make up the Langkawi archipelago. — Bernama

Title: National unity minister says Orang Asal heritage part of Malaysia’s national identity, not separate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The heritage of Malaysia’s indigenous peoples (Orang Asal) is part of the country’s national legacy and identity, rather than belonging solely to the communities themselves, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said.
In a Facebook post marking the 2026 International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples today, he said efforts to empower indigenous communities should move in tandem with national development without allowing their languages, customs and traditional knowledge to become marginalised.
He said the country’s progress should provide more opportunities for indigenous youth to excel in education, the economy and leadership while preserving their cultural roots and identity.
“Malaysia is fortunate to have indigenous communities that are an important part of the country’s history and identity.
“The languages, arts, customs, traditional knowledge, relationship with nature and values passed down through generations are a significant part of Malaysia’s rich identity,” he said.
At the international level, Aaron said the United Nations (UN) recognised indigenous peoples as custodians and practitioners of unique cultural traditions and knowledge systems, including those related to environmental and biodiversity conservation.
According to him, in terms of national unity, indigenous communities are part of the Malaysian family, and the country’s diversity is a strength that shapes its identity rather than something that divides it.
“By respecting every community, preserving its heritage and valuing its contributions, we are building a more inclusive, harmonious and united country,” he said.
Aaron also urged all parties to renew their commitment to respecting indigenous identities, promoting their dignity and recognising their contributions to Malaysia.
“Their heritage is our shared heritage, and their identity forms part of Malaysia’s identity,” he said.
Observed annually on Aug 9, the International Day of the World’s Indigenous Peoples was designated by the UN General Assembly in 1994 through Resolution 49/214 to commemorate the first meeting of the United Nations Working Group on Indigenous Populations in 1982. — Bernama

Title: MBPP blames root rot and trunk cavity for Angsana collapse in George Town
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Root rot and a cavity in the base of a 90-year-old Angsana tree, compounded by chronic soil compaction and limited rooting space, contributed to its collapse along Jalan Macalister here today.
MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the 28-metre-tall tree, Pterocarpus indicus, had an estimated 30 per cent root rot, while cavity decay accounted for about 40 per cent of its base trunk.
“The collapse was caused by root rot estimated at around 30 per cent and base trunk cavities at about 40 per cent. These factors, combined with infrastructure upgrading works, chronic soil compaction, limited rooting space and the tree’s height, significantly increased the risk of structural failure,” he told Bernama today.
In the incident at about 9am, an elderly couple and their grandchild were injured when the Perodua Ativa sports utility vehicle (SUV) they were travelling in was crushed by the falling tree.
Rajendran said there were no reports of heavy rain or strong winds at or before the time of the incident.
He said MBPP began removing the fallen tree at 9.41am, with the road reopened at 2.20pm after clearing works were completed.
He said MBPP had assessed mature and aged trees along Jalan Macalister in 2024, resulting in 13 trees being identified for felling, all of which had since been removed.
He added that the last tree maintenance work along Jalan Macalister was carried out on January 29 this year, while a remote sensing study conducted last year found the trees along the road to be in good condition with no warning indicators.
He said 179 high-risk trees had been approved for felling this year, with 148 already removed, while 247 trees had been felled in the first three quarters.
MBPP says tree safety risks remain priority, especially those affected by works and restricted roots. — Picture via Facebook/Majlis Bandaraya Pulau Pinang
The trees were felled for various reasons, including obstructing drainage, being dead or leaning, posing a collapse risk, development projects, road and river widening, and encroaching on Penang Water Supply Corporation (PBAPP) pipeline alignments.
“For MBPP’s overall tree management programme, 2,535 trees were identified last year under various categories, including 45 cases involving drainage obstruction, 138 dead trees, 2,242 assessed under risk or other categories, and 110 linked to development or infrastructure works,” he said.
He said MBPP continues to prioritise trees posing safety risks, particularly those affected by infrastructure works and restricted rooting conditions.
“Following the incident, MBPP has instructed the appointed contractor to expedite work to reduce tree height and fell trees with potential collapse risks along Jalan Macalister, based on assessments by certified arborists,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak chokes under haze blanket as hot weather grips state until Aug 14
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 9 — Most parts of Sarawak will be experiencing hot weather and reduced rainfall until August 14, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip.
In addition, southern Sarawak is set to experience transboundary haze due to increased hotspots in the neighbouring country, he said.
“Analysis of the latest weather forecast models indicate that hot weather and below-average rainfall are expected in most parts of Borneo, including Sarawak, until August 14.
“The influence of southerly winds, combined with the anticipated high number of hot spots in the neighbouring country, could lead to transboundary haze and reduced visibility, particularly in southern Sarawak,” he said in a notice.
There are now eight locations in Sarawak where the monitoring stations recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings. — The Borneo Post

Title: Terengganu police arrest three Myanmar men over sexual offence against disabled woman
Article:
CHUKAI, Aug 9 — Three Myanmar male refugees working as construction and cleaning workers were detained in connection with a sexual case involving an intellectually disabled woman in this district yesterday.
Kemaman district police chief Supt Mohd Razi Mohd Rosli said the three men, aged between 19 and 28, were arrested after receiving a report regarding the alleged sexual case from a 20-year-old woman on Friday.
“All three suspects have been remanded from August 8 to 12 to assist in the investigation. The investigation is still ongoing to identify other suspects who may be involved,” he said in a statement today.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 376 of the Penal Code.
He said the police need to fine-tune the investigation and to give sufficient space and time to the 23-year-old victim before completing the probe, considering that the woman is an intellectually disabled person.
In addition, Mohd Razi said his team also detected the spread of a video on the TikTok social media platform at around 8.30pm yesterday, showing a crowd gathering in front of the Kampung Enjin Gergaji Flats here following allegations of a sexual offence linked to the suspects.
He said that the public is advised not to make any baseless speculation as the case is still under police investigation.
“The police also advised the public not to take hasty actions against Rohingya refugees that could lead to criminal acts,” he said.
Members of the public who have information related to the case can contact any nearby police station or call 09-859 2222 to connect to the investigating officer, Inspector Mohd Hadaza Mat Amin. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian tahfiz student killed, friend injured after motorcycle crashes into pole in Yala
Article:
YALA, Aug 9 — A Malaysian man was killed while his friend was seriously injured after the motorcycle they were riding was involved in an accident in the Bannang Sareng area, Mueang Yala district, on Saturday afternoon.
Mueang Yala Police Chief Col Chatchai Sakdee said preliminary investigations found that the victim lost control of the motorcycle before crashing into an electricity pole.
“The 20-year-old pillion rider from Perlis died at the scene from severe head injuries, while the 22-year-old rider from Kuala Kedah, Kedah, was seriously injured,” he said when contacted today.
Chatchai said the injured victim is currently receiving treatment in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) at Yala Central Hospital and remains unconscious.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Consulate in Songkhla, which confirmed the nationality of both victims, said it was still waiting for the next of kin to come forward to arrange the necessary documentation.
It is understood that both victims were Quranic tahfiz students at Pondok Padang Pusu in the Yarang District, Pattani, and were on their way to the institution before the accident occurred. — Bernama

Title: Police lodge report after fake statement linked to deputy IGP spreads on Facebook
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 9 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) has denied a viral social media post falsely linked to the deputy Inspector-General of Police (IGP), stressing that the content was fabricated and misleading.
The force said the post, shared via a Facebook account, carried visuals and text suggesting the deputy IGP had held a special press conference at Bukit Aman on a police operation.
“PDRM stresses that the post is fake. The deputy IGP has never held such a press conference or issued any statement as claimed,” the force said in a statement issued by DCP Datuk Mohamad Noor Yusof Ali, secretary of the Royal Malaysia Police.
The statement added that the content used false images and identity markers to create the impression it was an official position of PDRM.
“Such acts risk confusing the public, sparking misunderstanding and undermining the credibility of both the individual and the institution.”
Police confirmed a report has been lodged to enable a full investigation into those responsible for producing and spreading the post, including examining the motive behind its circulation.
“PDRM views seriously any attempt to fabricate, manipulate or disseminate false content using the identity, image or position of police officers to give the impression that a statement or action is official,” it said.
The public was advised not to believe or share unverified information and to seek confirmation through official PDRM channels and credible news sources.
“PDRM also urges society to be responsible social media users and not to engage in spreading content that could cause confusion or disrupt public order,” the statement added.

Title: Military veterans need more second-career opportunities, says Dr Wan Azizah
Article:
SERI KEMBANGAN, Aug 9 — The private sector needs to expand second-career opportunities for military veterans as part of efforts to strengthen their welfare and empowerment, says ‘Kempen Tabung Pahlawan’ (Warriors Fund Campaign) patron Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
She said the private sector also played an important role in ensuring military veterans got the opportunity to continue contributing to society and the nation after ending their service with the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF).
“I call on more parties to come forward and contribute to the Kempen Tabung Pahlawan, as well as veteran associations under the MAF Veterans’ Affairs Department (JHEV).
“Every sen contributed will go directly towards the welfare and wellbeing of our national heroes,” she said in her speech at the closing ceremony of the MyHeroes Golf Championship Cup 2026 (MYGCC 2026), organised by the Royal Malaysian Navy Veterans’ Association (PVTLDM), here today.
Also present were Navy chief Admiral Tan Sri Dr Zulhelmy Ithnain and PVTLDM president Commander (Rtd) Khairil Hariss Khairuddin, who is also MYGCC 2026 programme director.
A total of RM220,000 was raised from eight private companies through MYGCC 2026, in conjunction with Kempen Tabung Pahlawan, reinforcing the programme’s role as a fundraising platform for military veterans’ welfare.
Wan Azizah, who is also Bandar Tun Razak MP, said the government, through the MAF and JHEV, remained committed to safeguarding the welfare of military veterans and advancing their empowerment agenda.
She said records showed that public and corporate concern for Kempen Tabung Pahlawan continued to show positive growth.
“The contributions collected are used to support thousands of veterans and their dependants in terms of livelihood assistance, medical care, and education for the children of our heroes.
“This achievement is proof of the spirit of togetherness and the ethic of hard work without complacency, reflecting the principle of readiness to sacrifice that is upheld by every member of the Royal Malaysian Navy and the MAF,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Melaka seat swaps on the table for Perikatan, Samsuri tells BN
Article:
TAIPING, Aug 9 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is open to talks with Barisan Nasional (BN), including possible seat swaps, ahead of the Melaka state election, PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar reportedly said today.
Utusan Malaysia
reported Ahmad Samsuri as saying no formal discussions had taken place, but there was still sufficient time for the parties to consider electoral cooperation before the Melaka state assembly is dissolved.
“If BN is ready to discuss,
insya-Allah
, we are also ready to discuss,” he was quoted as saying after opening the 23rd Perak PAS Convention here.
He reportedly said PN was similarly prepared to hold talks with other Muafakat Nasional partners if they were willing to negotiate.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said yesterday that the coalition remained open to negotiations over seat allocations in Melaka, including possible swaps, but stressed that talks should be conducted in good faith and should not require parties to give up seats they had previously won.
Ahmad Samsuri said any discussions would ideally take place before the state assembly is dissolved to give the parties sufficient time to prepare for the election.
In the Negeri Sembilan state election, BN and PN formed an unofficial electoral pact, avoiding contests against each other in the same seats, with leaders from both coalitions also seen campaigning together.
Meanwhile, in Johor, BN and PN contested separately.

Title: Melaka Pakatan open to talks, coalition welcomes negotiations ahead state election
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 9 — Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to negotiations with any party for the upcoming Melaka State Election, said its chairman Adly Zahari.
He said the form of cooperation and number of seats to be contested have yet to be finalised, with two series of meetings held so far to assess the coalition’s prospects, while preparations for the state election remain focused internally within PH.
“In a democratic political system, various forms of cooperation can be implemented. We are discussing, but we have not made any decision at the PH level.
“We have not finalised the form of cooperation outside PH itself, but we certainly welcome anyone who wishes to hold negotiations,” he told reporters after officiating the Bukit Katil Santuni Madani Programme at the Melaka Tengah Vocational College field here today.
Adly said the coalition has also not held discussions with Melaka Barisan Nasional (BN), but remains open to working with parties that share aspirations aligned with the core principles and values of the Malaysia Madani agenda.
Commenting on seat targets, Adly said Melaka PH is optimistic about increasing its number of State Legislative Assembly seats from the five seats it previously won out of a total of 28.
He said assessments are being conducted based on PH’s strength in the three parliamentary constituencies it won, namely Alor Gajah, Kota Melaka and Hang Tuah Jaya, as well as its potential in Tangga Batu, Masjid Tanah and Jasin.
“Our primary focus is to increase our wins. We are very positive that we can indeed add to our core seats,” he said.
Meanwhile, Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) State Leadership Council (MPN) acting chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim said Melaka’s political situation has its own distinct dynamics compared with other states forming the Unity Government, meaning all factors must be considered in any negotiations.
“Officially, there are no formal negotiations with BN yet, but communication and discussions are ongoing. Individually and as party representatives with BN, we will look for ways to resolve matters,” he said.
Adam Adli added that for now, PH state assemblymen are focusing on fulfilling their duties and responsibilities to the public while avoiding excessive political polemics that could disrupt social consensus and unity. — Bernama

Title: Driver forgot to put SUV in park before crashing into KKIA departure hall, police say
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — Police said preliminary investigations indicate that a 66-year-old woman forgot to put her SUV in parking gear before it rolled forward and crashed into the glass doors of Kota Kinabalu International Airport’s (KKIA) departure hall on Friday.
Berita Harian
reported Kota Kinabalu police chief ACP Shahrudin Mat Husain as saying the woman had stopped in the airport’s second lane to pick up her child and was preparing to switch drivers when the incident occurred.
“Preliminary investigations found that the woman is believed to have forgotten to put the vehicle’s gear in ‘P’ while changing drivers. As she tried to get out, the SUV began moving slowly, causing her to panic before she accidentally stepped on the accelerator,” he said.
Shahrudin said the SUV then surged forward, struck another vehicle and crashed through the departure hall’s glass doors before hitting a building pillar.
The woman managed to get out of the SUV before the collision but suffered minor facial injuries from glass fragments and was taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital I for treatment.
No passengers or airport staff were injured in the incident.
Police are investigating the case under Rule 10 of the Road Traffic Rules 1959 under the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Samsuri says Bersatu remains in Perikatan despite Hadi’s claim
Article:
TAIPING, Aug 9 — Bersatu remains a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) despite claims that its membership had automatically lapsed over plans for a new political coalition, PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar reportedly said today.
Utusan Malaysia
reported Ahmad Samsuri as saying Bersatu’s status in PN had not changed as of today.
“As of today, they are still a member of Perikatan Nasional,” he was quoted as saying after opening the 23rd Perak PAS Convention here.
Asked about Bersatu’s plan to lodge a report with the Registrar of Societies (RoS), Ahmad Samsuri said the party was free to take whatever action it considered appropriate as long as it complied with the law and existing rules.
PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang had on Friday claimed that Bersatu was no longer part of PN after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition.
He said the PN constitution stipulated that a member party would automatically cease to be part of the coalition if it joined or established another alliance.
Bersatu has rejected the claim, maintaining that it remains a PN component party and has yet to decide whether to join any other political coalition, including Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR).

Title: Umno‑PAS pact not for Sabah, Salleh Keruak says politics driven by autonomy rights
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — Any political understanding between Umno and PAS that may work in Peninsular Malaysia may not necessarily be suitable for Sabah, where political realities are markedly different, said Umno Sabah treasurer Datuk Seri Salleh Said Keruak.
He said the 2025 Sabah State Election had clearly demonstrated the strength of Sabah-based political sentiment, with local interests, autonomy, development and Sabah’s rights increasingly influencing voters’ choices.
“Malaysia is one country, but that does not mean every state must adopt the same political or electoral formula,” he said in a post on his Facebook page on Sunday.
Salleh said Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) won 29 of the 55 seats it contested in the state election, while Parti Warisan (Warisan) secured 25 of the 73 seats it contested.
He said GRS and Warisan together held 54 of the 73 seats in the Sabah State Legislative Assembly, while five other seats were won by independent candidates who subsequently supported the formation of a GRS-led state government.
“Viewed as a whole, the vast majority of successful candidates came from Sabah-based parties, local coalitions or independents whose politics are centred on Sabah’s interests.
“They may not form a single political bloc, but the results clearly demonstrate the strength of Sabah-centric politics,” he said.
Salleh noted that Barisan Nasional (BN) won six seats, Perikatan Nasional (PN) one, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) suffered a significant decline, winning only one seat.
He said the situation in Sarawak provided an even clearer example, with Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) strengthening its position through a political approach centred on Sarawak’s interests, while Umno had never established a foothold there.
“Therefore, any Umno-PAS understanding that may prove effective in Peninsular Malaysia may not necessarily be suitable for implementation in Sabah.
“It could even have the opposite effect if it is perceived as a political formula that is overly centred on Peninsular Malaysia,” he said.
Salleh said Umno Sabah should instead be viewed as a national party that understood the state’s political realities and was prepared to work closely with Sabah-based parties, particularly GRS.
“The formula must be clear: political stability, development, Sabah’s rights and the interests of the people of Sabah,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: DAP congress set for Aug 16 showdown, stalled reforms and grassroots frustration to dominate agenda
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 9 — National DAP organising secretary Datuk Chan Foong Hin said concerns over the lack of progress on institutional reforms, partly due to insufficient parliamentary support, will be addressed at the party’s national congress on August 16.
He said the annual congress, which will involve more than 4,000 delegates, would provide an opportunity for members to assess the party’s direction after three and a half years in government amid growing dissatisfaction at the grassroots level.
Chan acknowledged that several key reforms, including a proposed 10-year limit for the prime minister’s tenure and the separation of the roles of Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, had not been implemented due to insufficient support in Parliament.
“Without adequate support, it is difficult to carry out major reforms,” he said, questioning the absence of BN backbenchers.
He said the congress would include debates and a vote on the party’s direction, stressing that this was not a reaction to recent political developments but part of DAP’s internal democratic process.
Chan also described Malaysia’s current political landscape as “blurred”, citing recent political developments in Peninsular Malaysia following state election results, including the appearance of opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin alongside figures aligned with the ruling bloc.
He said that Sabah is a completely different situation altogether, where party positions remain more clearly defined despite election outcomes.
He stressed the need to balance political clarity with maintaining enough parliamentary support to pass reforms and the federal budget.
“The key question is what we want to achieve in the remaining term,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak haze thickens, Serian tops API at 170 as Kuching, Bintulu readings hit 155
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 9 — Miri and Sarikei recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 1pm today.
According to the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), eight districts are now recording unhealthy API levels, including Miri (118) and Sarikei (147).
Serian remains the highest at 170, followed by Samarahan (156). Kuching and Bintulu recorded 155 each, while Sri Aman and Samalaju registered 153 each.
Other monitoring stations across the state recorded moderate API readings, ranging from 74 to 92.
An API reading between 101 and 200 is categorised as unhealthy and may pose health risks to sensitive groups, including children, the elderly, and individuals with respiratory conditions. — The Borneo Post

Title: Malaysia Day 2026 celebration set for Kuching’s Borneo Convention Centre, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The 2026 Malaysia Day celebration will be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the decision was reached during the first preparatory meeting for the event last Monday, held with Sarawak Minister for Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah, who is co-chairman of this year’s Malaysia Day celebrations.
“We have assessed the venue and it is suitable in terms of space. It is almost identical to the PICCA Convention Centre in Butterworth, where we held the Malaysia Day celebration last year,” he told reporters after the Japen@Petronas Jalur Gemilang Expression Programme here today.
Fahmi said preparations for the Malaysia Day celebration were progressing smoothly, with the next meeting scheduled for August 24 to further discuss arrangements for the event.
Meanwhile, he said Prasarana Malaysia Bhd has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with the National Day celebration in Putrajaya on August 31.
He said the measure was an improvement over previous years and was expected to make it easier for the public to travel to Putrajaya and return home after the celebration.
“We also take note that several other infrastructure facilities will be improved. We hope this will help more people not only to come to Putrajaya, but also to head home after the National Day event concludes,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Three freed after fallen tree traps them inside car in George Town
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 9 — Three people were rescued after a tree fell on the Perodua Ativa they were travelling in along Jalan Macalister this morning.
The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 9.12am and dispatched eight firefighters from the Jalan Perak Fire and Rescue Station to the scene.
“All three victims who were trapped inside the vehicle were successfully freed by members of the public before the rescue team arrived,” the department said.
Firefighters later carried out work to cut up and remove the fallen tree and debris to ensure public safety and ease traffic flow.
The department said further information on the victims’ condition would be provided when available.

Title: Prasarana to run 24-hour public transport services for National Day, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad will operate public transport services around the clock from the night of August 30 into August 31 for this year’s National Day celebrations, Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil reportedly said today.
Berita Harian
reported Fahmi as saying the move was intended to make it easier for the public to travel to and from Putrajaya for the celebrations.
“Prasarana has committed to providing 24-hour public transport services in conjunction with National Day 2026,” he was quoted as saying.
“We hope this will not only help more people get to Putrajaya, but also make it easier for them to return home after the programme ends.”
Fahmi also said that this year’s Malaysia Day celebration on September 16 would be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) in Kuching, Sarawak.

Title: Minister warns unregistered marriages risk children’s rights, complicate birth certificates, education
Article:
LABUAN, Aug 9 — Unregistered marriages can have serious implications on children’s rights and family welfare, including difficulties in obtaining birth certificates, accessing education and healthcare, as well as inheritance matters, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.
He said there were still couples who had been living as husband and wife for decades without registering their marriages, while some had married outside their area or through unauthorised marriage registrars without complying with the procedures stipulated under the Islamic Family Law (Federal Territories) Act 1984 (Act 303).
“The implications of failing or delaying marriage registration are not a small matter. The effects are significant and far-reaching,” he said when launching the 2026 Federal Territories Syariah Law Literacy Programme at Kompleks Darul Kifayah here today.
Zulkifli said children were among those who could be most affected by unregistered marriages, as the situation could complicate the process of obtaining birth certificates and expose them to difficulties in accessing education and healthcare, as well as issues relating to identity and citizenship.
He said the absence of official marriage registration could also raise doubts regarding the status of a child’s lineage, while wives could face difficulties in claiming maintenance (nafkah) or ‘mutaah’.
“Matters involving inheritance and ‘faraid’ can also become complicated and trigger family disputes when a death occurs,” he said.
Zulkifli said the department, together with religious agencies and strategic partners, was taking a proactive approach to addressing outstanding marriage registration and marriage verification issues among residents.
“We are here not to find fault or punish anyone, but to help, facilitate and resolve these issues comprehensively for the future of families and children,” he said.
He urged those with outstanding marriage registration issues or doubts concerning marriage laws to approach officers at the interactive counters provided during the programme.
“Do not be ashamed and do not be afraid,” he said.
Zulkifli said marriage registration was important to ensure that a union was officially recognised and to safeguard the rights and interests of spouses and children.
He said compliance with syariah law should not be viewed as a burden but as a form of protection that could prevent disputes and safeguard the future of families.
The programme, organised by the Federal Territories Syariah Prosecution Department, involves the cooperation of various agencies, including the Labuan Member of Parliament’s Office, Federal Territories Syariah Court, Federal Territories Islamic Religious Department (Jawi), Federal Territories Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP), Legal Aid Department, Federal Territories Mufti Department, Tabung Haji and Yayasan Pembangunan Ekonomi Islam Malaysia (YAPEIM). — Bernama

Title: Malaysia awaits US response on excess capacity after concluding forced-labour tariff talks, says Johari Ghani
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 9 — Malaysia is awaiting Washington’s response on concerns over industrial excess capacity after completing the forced-labour component of its discussions with the US, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani today.
The Star
reported that Johari, speaking at the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia’s (ACCCIM) 80th annual general meeting here, said the government would continue engaging the US on the outstanding issue.
“We have finalised the forced-labour component. The issue of excess capacity has not been concluded yet,” he was quoted as saying.
“We are waiting for a response and will provide an update once received,” he reportedly added.
The US imposed an additional 10 per cent Section 301 tariff on Malaysian goods, subject to exemptions, from July 24 following its investigation into Malaysia’s rules on imports linked to forced labour, while a separate investigation into structural excess capacity remains unresolved.
Under the Malaysia-US Agreement on Reciprocal Trade, Malaysia has committed to prohibit imports made using forced labour as well as take steps to address global excess capacity in the steel sector.
Johari also reportedly said Malaysia’s exports to the US continued to grow, but cautioned against allowing imports to rise faster and weaken the country’s trade surplus.

Title: Myanmar refugee figures soon, Saifuddin Nasution vows biometric drive for repatriation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — Preliminary data on Myanmar refugees who are currently identified through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme is expected to be obtained in the fourth quarter of this year, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the Home Ministry (KDN) through the Immigration Department (JIM) is implementing the data collection process with relevant parties.
“I expect we will obtain the first data in the fourth quarter of this year, now it is August. Whatever the number is, I will share it with the media later,” he said in a press conference after the Star City FC Tour Convoy flag off ceremony here today.
The media reported that KDN through JIM is implementing the DPP programme to manage the issue of this group in an organised manner, in line with National Security Council Directive No. 23 (Revision 2023).
KDN said the programme was created to enable the government to obtain more accurate, complete and verifiable biometric data and identity information on individuals in the refugee category.
Saifuddin Nasution said individuals identified as refugees would be given priority for repatriation through action by Wisma Putra.
“If they are legitimate refugees, then they will certainly be among the first groups we will manage to repatriate. That will be handled by Wisma Putra.
“We are conducting a data collection. We need to have a mechanism to reach out to them and publicise that the Malaysian Government is conducting a data collection and we will ask them to come forward,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution explained that the refugee data collection is not focused on Myanmar refugees only but covers all those identified in this country. — Bernama

Title: 'Wishing them a speedy recovery': Anwar visits Ismail Sabri and Fadillah at IJN
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Amar Fadillah Yusof and former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, who are both receiving treatment at the National Heart Institute (IJN), yesterday.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said he made the visits with his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.
“Azizah and I pray that both of them are granted a speedy recovery, that all aspects of their treatment are eased, and that they continue to be blessed with good health and strength to continue serving the people and the country,
insya-Allah
,” he said.
Fadillah’s office announced on August 3 that he would undergo heart bypass surgery at IJN on the advice of medical specialists, with his condition then reported to be stable.
Ismail Sabri, meanwhile, was admitted to IJN on August 6 after experiencing health issues while having his statement recorded at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission headquarters.
He underwent a successful leadless pacemaker implantation procedure for an abnormal heart rhythm the following day and remained under close monitoring at IJN.

Title: Pakatan hails BN openness, Fahmi says Melaka seat talks offer chance for stability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) welcomes the openness of Barisan Nasional (BN) regarding the distribution of seats for the upcoming Melaka state election and describes it as an opportunity that deserves to be examined.
PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the openness should also be accepted for the future and political stability of Melaka, in addition to its importance to the country.
“The chairman of Keadilan Melaka, Yang Berhormat Adam Adli, also informed that he had been in direct contact with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusof (regarding the distribution of Melaka State Legislative Assembly seats).
“I think this openness is a good opportunity for us to examine because we know that in Melaka, BN has 21 seats, while PH has five seats. So that is a realistic matter,” he told reporters after officiating the Gotong-royong Mega Perangi Aedes programme in the Lembah Pantai area, here today.
Fahmi, who is also the Communications Minister, said in this regard several matters could be managed at the state and federal levels regarding the distribution of state seats in Melaka.
Yesterday, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition was still open to negotiations regarding the distribution, or even the exchange of seats, to face the Melaka state election, as long as it was done honestly and sincerely and did not affect the number of seats for each party.
Ahmad Zahid also said the basic principle of the negotiations was that the seats won by any party must be respected and not simply handed over to political partners. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution vows scanner upgrade, promises smarter baggage checks after pilot drug scandal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 9 — The government will look into upgrading scanning machines at airports nationwide as part of efforts to strengthen security and improve the effectiveness of baggage screening, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the government was always open to exploring the use of the latest screening equipment in line with technological advancements, particularly at the country’s main entry points.
He added that the existing scanning machines at airports were functioning well and had a high capability to detect dangerous items and other prohibited materials.
“Are we going to remain static with the existing machines going forward? Certainly not, because there are various types of equipment available for airport entry-point screening that are far more advanced and have greater capabilities.
“We are always open to ideas on adopting all types of new equipment,” he said at a press conference after the flag-off ceremony for the Star City FC Tour Convoy here today.
Airport security control has come under scrutiny following several recent cases involving Malaysians, including the detention of a Malaysian pilot after about 25 kilogrammes of MDMA-type drugs were seized at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Indonesia last week.
Saifuddin Nasution said baggage screening at airports was the responsibility of the Aviation Security (AVSEC) team and was in line with international airport screening standards under the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).
In this regard, he said improvements to the scope of baggage screening were also being considered to enable prohibited items, including drugs being smuggled, to be detected.
“From the perspective of the screening scope, the focus (currently) is more on weaponry than contraband. We see this as one of the areas for improvement that we need to focus on, in line with the expertise of the officers conducting the screening,” he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said he and agencies under the Home Ministry would hold a special meeting tomorrow to examine the implementation of a comprehensive plan to improve security controls at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
“Home Ministry and Transport Ministry have been asked to submit a comprehensive improvement plan aimed at mitigating incidents in terms of operations, equipment and manpower,” he said.
Earlier, Saifuddin Nasution said the Cabinet had instructed the Home Ministry and the Transport Ministry to submit a comprehensive plan to improve security controls at KLIA within two weeks.
He said the directive followed the government’s concerns over the latest incident, which was viewed as potentially tarnishing the country’s image as well as creating a perception that there were weaknesses in the security control system at the premises. — Bernama

Title: Bersatu turns to RoS after Hadi says party automatically out of Perikatan
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 9 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) reportedly plans to lodge a report with the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over claims that its Perikatan Nasional (PN) membership had automatically lapsed after the party expressed its intention to form a new political coalition.
Utusan Malaysia
reported Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz as saying that PN, which he claimed was now dominated by PAS, should be governed according to its constitution and principles of good governance, rather than the interests of any one party.
“PAS’ repeated actions in breaching the PN constitution and decisions of the PN Supreme Council, including denying the rights of member parties, should be reported to the RoS so that this can be stopped immediately,” he was quoted as saying.
“The PN chairman now appears to be a puppet. The centre of power is in Rusila, and the PAS president can arbitrarily question and breach decisions of the PN Supreme Council and do as he pleases.
“PN is not PAS. PN must be managed in accordance with the PN constitution, fairly, transparently and with integrity, without denying the rights of its members. PN must be restored to what it originally was,” he reportedly added.
On Friday, PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang claimed Bersatu’s PN membership had automatically lapsed after its president, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, announced plans to form a new political coalition.
He said the PN constitution stipulated that a member would cease to belong to the coalition upon joining another alliance.
Bersatu, however, maintained that its position in PN remained unchanged as it had yet to decide whether to join any other political coalition, including Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR).

Title: Govt ends 40-year settlement issue with land grants for 120 Perak families, says housing minister
Article:
IPOH, Aug 9 — A total of 120 squatter families around Sungkai and Kuala Bikam have been given land grants, resolving a settlement issue they had faced for more than 40 years, says Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
In a statement last night, Nga said the resolution of the issue was proof that the Madani Government always prioritised the wellbeing of the people regardless of racial background and social status, in line with its commitment to ensuring no Malaysian was left behind or marginalised in development.
“The squatter problem that has dragged on for more than 40 years can finally be resolved. Last night, 120 families are receiving land grants that symbolise a more secure future for them and future generations,” he said.
The DAP national deputy chairman said this when presenting the land grants to recipients at a dinner organised by the DAP Sungkai state constituency division last night, which was attended by more than 1,200 guests from various communities.
He also expressed appreciation to Sungkai assemblyman and state Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan, as well as all civil servants who worked tirelessly and with dedication to ensure the issue was resolved.
Nga said the Madani Government's commitment to the Indian community was also reflected in various initiatives, including RM20 million allocated for Indian settlements, RM50 million for Tamil vernacular schools (SJKTs) and an increase in the allocation for the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (MITRA) to RM150 million.
“These are among the proofs that the Madani Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is constantly striving to build an inclusive, fair and equitable Malaysia, guided by the principle that no one is left behind or marginalised,” he said.
Meanwhile, Nga urged the people to assess the government's actual performance and achievements and not be swayed by racial sentiments.
“Let us not allow performance to lose out to perception. Our country needs a new, constructive politics, not an outdated, destructive one.
“The politics of the future must be rooted in unity, performance-driven service, development and the wellbeing of the people,” he said.
Also present at the DAP Sungkai 60th anniversary dinner were Ipoh Timur MP Howard Lee Chuan How, Buntong assemblyman M. Thulsi, Malim Nawar assemblyman V. Bavani, Astaka assemblyman Jason Ng Thien Yong and other local community leaders. — Bernama

Title: Immigration investigates video of vehicle reportedly misusing department logo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 9 — The Immigration Department is investigating the use of its logo on a vehicle seen in a viral social media post and reportedly driven by a foreign national.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said preliminary checks found that the vehicle did not belong to the department and was not one of its official assets.
“The department takes seriously the use of its logo on the vehicle as it could cause confusion and create a false impression among members of the public,” he said in a statement today.
The department said investigations were under way to identify the individual involved and determine the purpose behind the use of its logo on the vehicle.
It said appropriate action would be taken under the relevant laws if any offence was found to have been committed.
Zakaria said the department would not compromise on any misuse of its logo or identity that could mislead the public or undermine its image and integrity.
He also urged the public to exercise caution when sharing information related to the case while investigations are ongoing.

Title: Perlis Umno gears up to contest all seats solo at next election
Article:
ARAU, Aug 9 — Perlis Umno is preparing its machinery to contest all 15 state seats and three parliamentary constituencies on its own at the next election, state liaison chairman Datuk Rozabil Abd Rahman reprotedly said.
Berita Harian
reported that Rozabil said there had so far been no official talks with any political party, including Perikatan Nasional (PN), on electoral cooperation in Perlis.
“What party members want, and what we have been working towards, is to continue working in all 15 state seats and three parliamentary constituencies,” he was quoted as saying last night.
He said the state chapter, which failed to win any seat in Perlis at the last election, would leave any eventual decision on electoral cooperation to the party’s national leadership.
Rozabil said some parties had approached him about meeting, but he considered such discussions premature and said the immediate priority was to ensure the party machinery continued working.
He also reportedly claimed the PN state administration had failed to deliver significant development, particularly economic opportunities and jobs for young people.
He said Umno’s machinery, including Wanita Umno’s Jalinan Rakyat network at polling districts, was already being mobilised as though an election could be held at any time.

Title: Five Sarawak areas record unhealthy API levels amid transboundary haze
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 9 — Five areas in Sarawak continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to transboundary haze as of 8am today, compared with six areas yesterday afternoon.
Based on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the areas recording unhealthy API readings were Kuching (153), Samarahan (156), Serian (170), Bintulu (156) and Samalaju (151).
Yesterday, Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas reportedly said that transboundary haze was expected to affect 19 areas in Sarawak over the next few days, with current wind patterns carrying smoke from hotspots in neighbouring regions into the state.
Uggah, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the areas identified were Betong, Bintulu, Daro, Julau, Kanowit, Kuching, Lundu, Marudi, Miri, Mukah, Pakan, Samarahan, Saratok, Serian, Sibu, Simunjan, Song, Sri Aman and Tatau. — Bernama
